newsitem.title: USA: Clark USA sees improved 1997 retail margins.
newsitem.headline: Clark USA sees improved 1997 retail margins.

text.p: Clark USA Inc said Tuesday it expects retail margins to improve in 1997 with a more stable crude oil price environment.
"Our cash position has never been stronger and we continue to explore alternatives for the best use of these funds," said chief executive Paul Melnuk.

The petroleum refiner and gasoline marketer reported a fourth-quarter net loss of $26.9 million, compared to a year-ago loss of $15.1 million. Quarterly revenues were $1.35 billion, up from $1.11 billion.
Clark is 46-percent owned by TrizecHahn Corp.
For the year, the company reported a net loss of $56.2 million, versus a 1995 loss of $37.1 million. Annual revenues were $5.07 billion, compared to $4.49 billion.
"The adverse impact of high and volatile oil prices masked what otherwise was excellent operating performance in our businesses this year," Melnuk said.

The fourth quarter contribution from the refining division improved over $10 million from 1995 and more than doubled for the year. Improved yields and throughput for the division offset the adverse impact of higher crude prices and downtime at the Blue Island refinery, the company said.

Productivity gains and "modest improvement in certain market indicators" helped the Port Arthur refinery contribute nearly $25 million in the fourth quarter, up from $7 million in the same period last year.

"The total contribution generated by Port Arthur since it was acquired less than two years ago now totals approximately $80 million. This translates to a payback of less than two years during the weakest industry conditions in over a decade," Clark said.

"In 1996, industry fundamentals began to have a positive impact on many key refining market indicators, including gasoline and distillate margins and crude oil quality spreads," Clark said. "However, these positive market trends were more than offset by reduced retail gasoline and byproduct margins caused by rising, volatile and high absolute crude oil prices. Volatile oil prices also increased the cost of crude oil acquisition activities."

In addition, Clark said higher natural gas prices increased operating expenses, primarily at the Port Arthur refinery, by approximately $6 million and $18 million for the quarter and 1996, respectively.
